questions.q: Which pattern lets you swap interchangeable algorithms, such as different fee calculations, behind one interface at runtime?
questions.w: Strategy encapsulates each algorithm in its own class and lets the context pick one, replacing long if/else or switch chains.

questions.q: A legacy payment class has the wrong method names for your interface and you cannot change it. Which pattern fits?
questions.w: Adapter wraps an incompatible class and translates calls to the interface the client expects.

questions.q: What is the Decorator pattern for?
o: Adds behaviour to an object by wrapping it, keeping the interface
Creates objects without naming their concrete class
Makes exactly one instance globally available
Defines the skeleton of an algorithm for subclasses
questions.w: Java's `BufferedInputStream` wrapping `FileInputStream` is the textbook example. Spring AOP proxies work in a similar wrapping spirit.

questions.q: Why is a classic hand-written Singleton often criticised?
o: It hides global state, hurts testability and needs thread-safety care
It uses far too much memory for each instance
It cannot be written in Java without reflection
It forces every class to use inheritance
questions.w: In Spring, singleton scope for beans gives the one-instance benefit while dependency injection keeps code testable.

questions.q: Which pattern notifies many dependants automatically when one object changes state?
questions.w: Observer decouples the subject from its listeners. Spring application events and message topics follow the same idea.

questions.q: A constructor has eight parameters, most optional. Which pattern improves readability?
questions.w: Builder sets only the needed fields with named steps and then calls `build()`, avoiding telescoping constructors.

questions.q: A request must pass through validation, authentication and logging handlers, each deciding whether to continue. Which pattern is this?
questions.w: Servlet filters and Spring Security's filter chain are real-world examples.

questions.q: What is the Template Method pattern?
o: A base class fixes the steps while subclasses override some of them
A class that creates families of related objects
An object that produces copies of itself on request
One class that hides a complex subsystem behind a simple API
questions.w: The superclass controls the order and subclasses fill in the variable parts. `JdbcTemplate` uses the same principle with callbacks.
